title: CPR / Not Breathing
summary: What to do if someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally.
warningSigns: Blue or grey lips or face
Collapse after chest pain or choking
steps: Call 112 immediately or ask someone nearby to call.
Place the person flat on their back on a firm surface.
Put the heel of one hand in the center of the chest and the other hand on top.
Push hard and fast in the center of the chest, about 100 to 120 compressions per minute.
If trained, give rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. If not trained, continue hands-only CPR.
Continue until help arrives, an AED is ready, or the person starts breathing normally.
doNot: Do not delay CPR while looking for a pulse if the person is not breathing normally.
Do not give food, drink, or medication.
Do not stop compressions unless the person recovers or help takes over.
seekCare: This is an emergency. Call 112 immediately.

title: Choking
summary: First aid for severe choking in adults and children over 1 year.
warningSigns: Cannot breathe, speak, cry, or cough
steps: If the person can cough, encourage them to keep coughing.
If they cannot breathe or speak, call 112 or ask someone to call.
Give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
If still choking and you are trained, give abdominal thrusts.
Alternate back blows and abdominal thrusts until the object comes out or help arrives.
If the person becomes unconscious, begin CPR.
doNot: Do not put your fingers in the mouth unless you can clearly see and remove the object.
Do not give water or food.
Do not slap the back if the person is coughing effectively.
seekCare: Seek medical care after severe choking, even if the object comes out.

title: Severe Bleeding
summary: Control heavy bleeding while waiting for emergency help.
warningSigns: Bleeding that does not slow with pressure
Pale, cold, weak, confused, or faint
steps: Call 112 for heavy or uncontrolled bleeding.
Apply firm direct pressure with clean cloth, gauze, or clothing.
Keep pressure steady. Add more cloth if blood soaks through.
If possible, raise the bleeding area above heart level.
Help the person lie down and keep them warm.
If trained and bleeding is life-threatening from an arm or leg, use a tourniquet above the wound.
doNot: Do not remove cloth already stuck to the wound.
Do not remove large embedded objects.
Do not repeatedly lift the dressing to check the wound.
seekCare: Urgent medical care is needed for heavy bleeding, deep wounds, bites, dirty wounds, or bleeding that does not stop.

title: Burns
summary: Cool burns quickly and know when urgent care is needed.
warningSigns: Burn on face, airway, hands, genitals, or large area
Trouble breathing after smoke or chemical exposure
White, charred, leathery, or numb skin
Burn caused by electricity or chemicals
steps: Move the person away from the heat source.
Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes.
Remove jewelry or tight clothing near the burn unless stuck to skin.
Cover with a clean non-stick dressing or clean cloth.
Keep the person warm and watch for shock.
Call 112 for serious burns or breathing problems.
doNot: Do not use ice directly on a burn.
Do not apply butter, oil, toothpaste, or powders.
Do not pop blisters.
Do not pull away clothing stuck to burned skin.
seekCare: Get medical care for deep, large, chemical, electrical, infected, or face/hand/genital burns.

title: Stroke Signs
summary: Use FAST signs and act immediately.
warningSigns: Sudden severe headache, vision loss, dizziness, or trouble walking
steps: Call 112 immediately. Stroke treatment is time-sensitive.
Note the time symptoms started or when the person was last normal.
Keep the person resting with head slightly raised.
Loosen tight clothing and monitor breathing.
If unconscious but breathing, place them on their side.
Prepare medical ID, medications, and allergy information.
doNot: Do not give food, drink, or medication.
Do not let the person drive.
Do not wait to see if symptoms improve.
seekCare: Call 112 immediately for any suspected stroke.

title: Heart Attack Signs
summary: Recognize warning signs and get emergency care quickly.
warningSigns: Chest pain, pressure, squeezing, or heaviness
Pain spreading to arm, jaw, back, neck, or stomach
Shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or dizziness
steps: Call 112 immediately.
Help the person sit and rest.
Loosen tight clothing and keep them calm.
If they have prescribed heart medicine, help them take it as directed.
If they become unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR.
Prepare Medical ID and medication information.
doNot: Do not let the person walk around or drive.
Do not ignore mild symptoms.
Do not give food or drink if they may need emergency treatment.
seekCare: Call 112 immediately for possible heart attack symptoms.

title: Seizure
summary: Protect the person during a seizure and know when to call help.
warningSigns: Injury, pregnancy, diabetes, or seizure in water
First known seizure or trouble breathing after
steps: Move nearby objects away to prevent injury.
Cushion the head with folded clothing.
Time the seizure.
After shaking stops, place the person on their side if breathing.
Stay with them until fully alert.
Call 112 if warning signs are present.
doNot: Do not hold the person down.
Do not put anything in their mouth.
Do not give food, drink, or medicine until fully awake.
seekCare: Call 112 if the seizure lasts over 5 minutes, repeats, causes injury, or is the first seizure.

title: Fainting
summary: Help someone who faints or feels about to faint.
warningSigns: Chest pain, shortness of breath, or irregular heartbeat
steps: Help the person lie flat on their back.
Raise their legs slightly if there is no injury.
Loosen tight clothing and provide fresh air.
Check breathing and responsiveness.
When awake, help them sit up slowly.
Call 112 if warning signs are present.
doNot: Do not give food or drink until fully awake.
Do not make them stand up quickly.
Do not ignore fainting with chest pain or breathing trouble.
seekCare: Seek medical care for unexplained, repeated, or injury-related fainting.

title: Fracture or Sprain
summary: Immobilize injuries and reduce swelling.
warningSigns: Bone visible or limb looks deformed
Severe pain, numbness, or loss of pulse
Head, neck, back, hip, or thigh injury
Unable to move or bear weight
steps: Keep the injured area still.
Support the limb in the position found.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 to 20 minutes.
Elevate if comfortable and safe.
Remove rings or tight items before swelling increases.
Seek medical care for suspected fracture or severe sprain.
doNot: Do not try to straighten a deformed limb.
Do not massage the injury.
Do not apply ice directly to skin.
seekCare: Call 112 for severe deformity, heavy bleeding, numbness, or head/neck/back injury.

title: Poisoning
summary: Respond to swallowed, inhaled, or skin contact poisons.
warningSigns: Severe vomiting or burns around mouth
Exposure to chemicals, drugs, or unknown substances
steps: Call 112 immediately for serious symptoms.
Move the person away from fumes if safe.
Remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin with water if exposed.
Keep the substance container or label for responders.
If the person vomits, turn their head to the side.
Follow emergency dispatcher instructions.
doNot: Do not make the person vomit unless told by medical professionals.
Do not give food, drink, or home remedies.
Do not enter a dangerous area with fumes.
seekCare: Poisoning can be life-threatening. Call 112 for serious or unknown exposure.

title: Severe Allergic Reaction
summary: Recognize anaphylaxis and act quickly.
warningSigns: Swelling of lips, tongue, throat, or face
Widespread hives with dizziness or vomiting
Collapse or confusion after allergen exposure
steps: Call 112 immediately.
Help the person use their prescribed epinephrine auto-injector if available.
Have them lie down with legs raised unless breathing is easier sitting up.
Loosen tight clothing.
If symptoms continue and a second auto-injector is prescribed, follow their plan.
Begin CPR if they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally.
doNot: Do not wait to see if severe symptoms improve.
Do not give food or drink.
Do not make them stand or walk around.
seekCare: Call 112 for any suspected anaphylaxis, even after epinephrine.

title: Heat Stroke
summary: Cool the person rapidly during dangerous overheating.
warningSigns: Hot skin, heavy sweating, or no sweating
steps: Call 112 immediately.
Move the person to shade or a cool place.
Remove excess clothing.
Cool rapidly with water, wet cloths, fan, or ice packs at neck, armpits, and groin.
If awake and able to swallow, give small sips of cool water.
Monitor breathing until help arrives.
doNot: Do not give alcohol or caffeine.
Do not give fluids if confused, vomiting, or unconscious.
Do not delay cooling while waiting for help.
seekCare: Heat stroke is an emergency. Call 112.

title: Asthma Attack
summary: Support breathing and know when it is an emergency.
warningSigns: Severe shortness of breath or cannot speak full sentences
steps: Help the person sit upright and stay calm.
Help them use their rescue inhaler as prescribed.
Loosen tight clothing.
Move away from smoke, dust, or trigger if possible.
Call 112 if symptoms are severe or not improving.
Be ready to start CPR if they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally.
doNot: Do not make the person lie flat if breathing is difficult.
Do not leave them alone.
Do not delay emergency help if inhaler is not working.
seekCare: Call 112 for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips, confusion, or no improvement.

title: Diabetic Emergency
summary: Help someone with low blood sugar or diabetic collapse.
warningSigns: Very weak, sweaty, shaky, or pale
steps: If awake and able to swallow, give fast sugar such as glucose drink, juice, or regular soft drink.
Wait 10 to 15 minutes and monitor improvement.
If they improve, help them eat longer-lasting food if available.
If unconscious, having a seizure, or unable to swallow, call 112.
Place an unconscious breathing person on their side.
Prepare Medical ID, insulin, medication, or glucose meter information.
doNot: Do not give food or drink to someone unconscious or unable to swallow.
Do not give insulin unless it is part of their own plan and they can manage it.
Do not leave them alone.
seekCare: Call 112 if unconscious, seizing, unable to swallow, or not improving.

title: Drowning
summary: Get the person out safely and support breathing.
warningSigns: Coughing foam or trouble breathing after water rescue
steps: Call 112 immediately.
Only rescue if it is safe. Use a pole, rope, or flotation aid if possible.
Once out of water, check breathing.
If not breathing normally, start CPR.
If breathing, place on side and keep warm.
Monitor closely until help arrives.
doNot: Do not put yourself in danger during rescue.
Do not assume the person is fine after coughing up water.
Do not delay CPR if not breathing normally.
seekCare: Anyone with breathing difficulty after drowning needs urgent medical care.

title: Electric Shock
summary: Make the scene safe before touching the person.
warningSigns: Chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or breathing trouble
steps: Do not touch the person until the power source is off.
Call 112 for serious shock or high-voltage exposure.
Turn off electricity if safe, or move the source with a dry non-conductive object.
Check breathing and responsiveness.
Start CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally.
Cover burns with a clean dry cloth.
doNot: Do not touch the person while they are still connected to electricity.
Do not use wet objects near electricity.
Do not apply ointments to electrical burns.
seekCare: Electrical injuries need medical review, especially with burns, chest pain, fainting, or high voltage.

title: Snake Bite
summary: Keep still and get urgent medical help.
warningSigns: Bite from unknown or venomous snake
steps: Call 112 or go to emergency care immediately.
Keep the person still and calm.
Keep the bitten limb below heart level if possible.
Remove rings, watches, or tight clothing near the bite.
Mark the edge of swelling and time if safe.
Describe the snake only if it can be done safely.
doNot: Do not cut the wound or suck out venom.
Do not apply ice.
Do not use a tight tourniquet.
Do not try to catch the snake.
seekCare: Snake bite requires urgent medical assessment.

title: Eye Injury
summary: Protect the eye and rinse chemicals immediately.
warningSigns: Blood in the eye or eye cut
steps: For chemicals, rinse the eye with clean running water for at least 15 minutes.
Remove contact lenses if they come out easily while rinsing.
For an object stuck in the eye, cover both eyes loosely and seek urgent care.
Keep the person from rubbing the eye.
Seek medical care for pain, vision change, or injury.
Call 112 for severe trauma or chemical exposure with serious symptoms.
doNot: Do not rub the eye.
Do not remove an embedded object.
Do not apply pressure to the injured eye.
Do not use eye drops after chemical exposure unless told by a professional.
seekCare: Urgent care is needed for chemical exposure, embedded objects, severe pain, or vision changes.

title: Shock
summary: Support circulation after serious injury, bleeding, burns, allergic reaction, or illness.
warningSigns: Thirst, nausea, or restlessness after injury or illness
steps: Call 112 immediately if shock is suspected.
Help the person lie flat on their back if comfortable.
Raise legs slightly if there is no head, neck, spine, hip, or leg injury.
Control any bleeding with direct pressure.
Keep the person warm with a cloth or blanket.
Monitor breathing and responsiveness until help arrives.
doNot: Do not give food or drink.
Do not move the person if you suspect spine, hip, or leg injury.
Do not let the person stand or walk around.
seekCare: Shock can be life-threatening. Call 112.

title: Head, Neck, or Spinal Injury
summary: Keep the person still and protect the spine after serious falls, crashes, or head trauma.
warningSigns: Fall from height, road crash, diving injury, or heavy blow
Confusion, vomiting, seizure, or loss of consciousness
steps: Call 112 immediately for suspected spine injury.
Tell the person to stay still and avoid moving the head or neck.
Support the head in the position found if safe to do so.
Keep airway open without tilting the head unless needed for breathing.
Control bleeding with gentle pressure around, not directly on, obvious skull injury.
Monitor breathing until help arrives.
doNot: Do not move the person unless there is immediate danger.
Do not twist or straighten the head or neck.
Do not remove a helmet unless airway access is impossible.
seekCare: Call 112 for suspected head, neck, or spinal injury.

title: Concussion
summary: Watch for brain injury symptoms after a blow to the head.
warningSigns: Loss of consciousness, seizure, or repeated vomiting
Unequal pupils, weakness, numbness, or slurred speech
Neck pain or suspected spine injury
steps: Stop activity and have the person rest.
Check for warning signs and call 112 if present.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth to swelling for short periods.
Keep the person with a responsible adult for observation.
Avoid alcohol, driving, sports, or risky activity until medically cleared.
Seek medical advice for any suspected concussion.
doNot: Do not let the person return to sport or work immediately.
Do not give sedatives or alcohol.
Do not ignore symptoms that worsen over time.
seekCare: Get medical advice for suspected concussion. Call 112 for severe or worsening symptoms.

title: Nosebleed
summary: Use forward leaning and steady pressure to control most nosebleeds.
warningSigns: Bleeding after serious head or face injury
Bleeding that lasts longer than 20 minutes
Person takes blood thinners or has bleeding disorder
steps: Have the person sit upright and lean forward.
Pinch the soft part of the nose just below the bridge.
Hold steady pressure for 10 to 15 minutes without checking.
Ask the person to breathe through the mouth.
Apply a cold cloth to the bridge of the nose if helpful.
Seek care if bleeding continues or warning signs are present.
doNot: Do not tilt the head back.
Do not pack the nose deeply.
Do not blow or pick the nose after bleeding stops.
seekCare: Seek care for heavy, repeated, injury-related, or prolonged nosebleeds.

title: Hypothermia
summary: Warm the person gradually after dangerous cold exposure.
warningSigns: Shivering that stops or becomes weak
Cold pale skin after cold water or weather exposure
steps: Call 112 for moderate or severe hypothermia.
Move the person to a warm, dry place if safe.
Remove wet clothing and cover with dry blankets or clothing.
Warm the center of the body first: chest, neck, head, and groin.
Give warm sweet drinks only if fully awake and able to swallow.
Monitor breathing and start CPR if not breathing normally.
doNot: Do not warm arms and legs first.
Do not use direct high heat such as hot water or heating pads.
Do not give alcohol.
seekCare: Call 112 for confusion, severe shivering, drowsiness, or cold-water exposure.

title: Dehydration
summary: Replace fluids and watch for heat illness or shock.
warningSigns: Very dry mouth, sunken eyes, or fast heartbeat
Baby or older adult with severe symptoms
steps: Move the person to a cool place and let them rest.
Give small frequent sips of water or oral rehydration solution.
Loosen tight clothing and cool with wet cloths if overheated.
For vomiting, give very small sips often.
Watch for heat stroke signs such as confusion or collapse.
Seek medical care if symptoms are severe or not improving.
doNot: Do not give large amounts quickly if vomiting.
Do not give alcohol.
Do not give fluids to someone unconscious or unable to swallow.
seekCare: Call 112 for confusion, fainting, severe weakness, or signs of heat stroke.

title: Infant Choking
summary: First aid for severe choking in babies under 1 year.
steps: Call 112 or ask someone nearby to call.
Support the baby face down along your forearm with the head lower than the chest.
Give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
Turn the baby face up while supporting the head.
Give up to 5 chest thrusts with two fingers on the center of the chest.
Repeat back blows and chest thrusts until the object comes out or help arrives.
doNot: Do not use abdominal thrusts on an infant.
Do not sweep the mouth blindly.
Do not shake the baby.
seekCare: Call 112 for severe infant choking. Seek medical care after the episode.

title: Internal Bleeding
summary: Recognize hidden bleeding after trauma or severe illness.
warningSigns: Severe pain, swelling, or bruising after injury
Black or bloody stool or urine
Pale, cold, weak, dizzy, confused, or faint
steps: Call 112 immediately if internal bleeding is suspected.
Help the person lie still and rest.
Treat for shock by keeping them warm.
Monitor breathing and responsiveness.
If vomiting, turn the head to the side if safe.
Share injury details and medications with responders.
doNot: Do not give food or drink.
Do not move the person unnecessarily.
Do not ignore worsening pain, weakness, or confusion after injury.
seekCare: Internal bleeding is an emergency. Call 112.

title: Animal Bite
summary: Clean minor bites and seek care for deep, dirty, or risky wounds.
warningSigns: Bite to face, hand, neck, or genitals
Animal may have rabies or cannot be identified
Increasing redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or fever
steps: Move away from the animal safely.
For bleeding, apply direct pressure with clean cloth.
Wash minor bites with running water and soap for several minutes.
Cover with a clean dressing.
Seek medical care for deep bites, dirty wounds, or rabies risk.
Report dangerous or stray animal bites to local authorities where appropriate.
doNot: Do not ignore bites that break the skin.
Do not close a deep bite wound yourself.
Do not approach or try to capture a dangerous animal.
seekCare: Seek care for any bite that breaks skin, deep wounds, infection signs, or possible rabies exposure.

title: Insect Sting
summary: Treat local reactions and watch for severe allergy.
warningSigns: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat
Dizziness, fainting, vomiting, or widespread hives
Multiple stings or sting in mouth/throat
steps: Move away from the insect area.
Remove a visible stinger by scraping sideways with a card or fingernail.
Wash the area with soap and water.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for pain and swelling.
Watch for severe allergic reaction signs.
Call 112 and use prescribed epinephrine if severe allergy signs appear.
doNot: Do not squeeze the venom sac if removing a stinger.
Do not scratch the sting.
Do not delay emergency help for breathing or swelling symptoms.
seekCare: Call 112 for severe allergic reaction. Seek care for infection, many stings, or mouth/throat sting.

title: Opioid Overdose
summary: Use naloxone if available and support breathing while waiting for help.
warningSigns: Blue or grey lips or fingernails
steps: Call 112 immediately.
Give naloxone if available and follow the product instructions.
Try to keep the person awake and breathing.
Place the person on their side if breathing.
Start CPR if they are not breathing normally.
Stay with the person. Give another naloxone dose if instructed and symptoms continue.
doNot: Do not leave the person alone.
Do not give food, drink, or stimulants.
Do not put the person in a bath or shower.
Do not wait to call emergency services.
seekCare: Opioid overdose is an emergency. Call 112 even if naloxone works.
